title: Reported Speech: Tomorrow and Time Expressions — Quiz 129
content:
## Reported Speech: Tomorrow and Time Expressions

Practise changing tomorrow and starting time expressions into reported speech.

### Lesson focus

1. The Principal said, “Students, a new English teacher is joining us tomorrow.”
2. Rohit said, “Mother, I'm starting the day after tomorrow.”

### Understand the pattern

Tomorrow is the day after the original speaker's today. When you report the message on a later date, the following day is clearer. Likewise, the day after tomorrow can become two days later; a calendar date can be clearer still.

### Worked answers and explanation

1. The principal told the students that a new English teacher was joining them the following day.
2. Rohit told his mother that he was starting two days later.

The continuous forms can describe planned future events. Do not change them into a different plan simply because the report uses a past reporting verb.

### Try another

Report later: She said, 'The meeting is tomorrow.'

### Suggested answer

She said that the meeting was the following day. If reporting on the same day, tomorrow may still correctly identify the intended date.
